en: Obeisance to Śrī Gaṇeśa. Ahalyā said:
"O Abode of the Universe, oh, I have achieved my life's purpose through even a single particle of dust clinging to Your lotus feet!"
I touch that which is sought after by Brahmā, Śaṅkara, and others, whose minds are ever-disciplined.

Oh, how wondrous is your activity, O Rāma! The world is deluded by your human nature; though you are devoid of feet and other limbs, you move eternally, you are full, composed of bliss, and beyond all illusion.
When she whose body is purified by the pollen of his lotus feet— the Bhāgīrathī who sanctifies even those headed by Śiva and Brahmā—
stands directly before my very eyes, how can my previously acquired good fortune be described?

I worship eternally Hari, who has assumed a human form in his descent among mortals, known by the name Rāma, possessing a beautiful body, wielding the bow, and having large eyes like lotuses; I shall never worship others.

I meditate incessantly in my heart upon that Rāmacandra, the dust of whose lotus feet is sought by the Vedas, who is the source of Brahmā and the one seated upon the lotus-throne, and who is the Lord Śiva, the enemy of Tripura, relishing the essence of whose name.

I take refuge in Him whose deeds of incarnation are sung in the world of Viriñci by the sons of Bhava and Padmaja, headed by Nārada, while Vāgīśvarī, the tips of whose breasts are moistened by tears born of bliss, likewise sings them. || 6 ||
This very Supreme Self, the ancient Puruṣa, who is self-luminous, infinite, and primordial—
this Rāma assumes a body of Māyā that deludes the world, solely for the sake of bestowing grace upon others.

For this one independent, perfect Self, reflected through the qualities of its own *māyā*, assumes the distinct names of Viriñci, Viṣṇu, and Īśvara among those who bring about the creation and dissolution of the universe. (8)

Homage be to you, O Rāma! Your lotus-feet, held upon the chest of Lakṣmī and cherished by her beloved, formerly traversed the three worlds alone; they are to be meditated upon by the lords of sages who are free from all pride.
You are the primordial source of the worlds, you are the world, and you are the refuge of the world;
unattached to all beings, you alone shine as the Supreme.
O Rāma, you are the Person who is signified by the syllable *oṃ* and yet remains beyond the reach of words;
through the distinction between the signified and the signifier, you alone are the one who comprises the entire universe.
O Rāma, though you are one, you appear manifold through your multiform Māyā, by means of the distinctions between cause and effect, agent and action, and the various instruments of accomplishment.
Those whose intellects are deluded by your māyā do not know you in reality;
they perceive you, the Supreme Lord who possesses māyā, as a mere human being. 13.
Like space, it is present everywhere; stainless, it exists both outside and within.
Indeed, it is unattached, immovable, eternal, pure, awakened, real, and imperishable.
O All-pervading Lord, I am a woman, deluded and ignorant; how then could I know the truth?
Therefore, O Rāma, with a mind focused on no other, I shall offer salutations to you hundreds of times.
O Lord, wherever I may dwell at any time,
may my devotion alone ever remain attached to Your lotus feet.
Salutations to you, O Supreme Overseer of all beings; salutations to you, O lover of your devotees.
Salutations be to you, O Hṛṣīkeśa; O Nārāyaṇa, let there be salutations unto you.

I praise Rāma together with his younger brother—he who alone removes the fear of worldly existence, who shines like ten million suns, who holds a bow and arrows in his hands, who has the luster of a dark rain cloud, who is clad in garments as beautiful as gold, who is adorned with jewel-studded earrings, and whose eyes are as clear as lotuses. 18.
Having thus praised the Supreme Person, Rāghava, who stood before her,
she circumambulated him, prostrated herself, and, having quickly received his permission, went to her husband.
Whoever recites this hymn composed by Ahalyā with devotion is liberated from all sins and attains the Supreme Brahman. (20)
For the sake of obtaining sons and other blessings, one should recite this with devotion while placing Rāma within the heart;
even a barren woman obtains a virtuous son within a year.
One obtains all desires through the grace of Rāmacandra. || 22 ||
Even a man who has killed a Brahmin, violated his guru’s bed, committed theft, or drunk liquor— even one who constantly harms his mother or brother and is solely devoted to sensual enjoyments—
by constantly reciting this hymn with devotion and remembering the Lord of the Raghus dwelling within his heart, [is purified].
If even one who merely meditates attains liberation, how much more so a man who is endowed with proper conduct? || 23 ||
Thus ends the hymn to Rāmacandra composed by Ahalyā in the glorious Adhyātmarāmāyaṇa.
